{{Short description|American biologist and philosopher (1939–2024)}}

'''Michael T. Ghiselin''' (born May 13, 1939; died June 14, 2024) was an American biologist and philosopher as well as a [[historian of biology]], formerly at the [[California Academy of Sciences]].

He is known for his work concerning [[sea slug]]s, and for his criticism of the falsification of the history of [[Lamarckism]] in biology textbooks.

== Academic life ==

Ghiselin received his B.A. in 1960 from the [[University of Utah]] and his Ph.D. from [[Stanford University]] in 1965. He became a Postdoctoral Fellow at [[Harvard University]] (1964–65) and later became Postdoctoral Fellow at the [[Marine Biological Laboratory]] in 1965. There he stayed until 1967 as he was appointed assistant professor of zoology at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] and later was chosen as a Guggenheim Fellow (1978–79). Ghiselin served as research professor of biology at the [[University of Utah]] (1980–83) and was [[MacArthur Fellows Program|MacArthur Prize Fellow]] from 1981 to 1986. From 1983 he was a senior research fellow at the [[California Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Academy Fellows |url=http://www.calacademy.org/scientists/academy-fellows |website=Calacademy.org |accessdate=20 March 2017}}</ref>

== Career ==

Ghiselin is famous for his work on [[sea slug]]s,<ref>{{cite journal |title=Chemical defense and evolutionary ecology of dorid nudibranchs and some other opisthobranch gastropods |author=D. John Faulkner and Michael T. Ghiselin |journal=Marine Ecology Progress Series |volume=13 |issue=2/3 |date=30 August 1983 |pages=295––301 |jstor=24815885|bibcode=1983MEPS...13..295F |doi=10.3354/meps013295 |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref name="CiminoGhiselin1998">{{cite journal |last1=Cimino |first1=Guido |last2=Ghiselin |first2=Michael T. |title=Chemical defense and evolution in the Sacoglossa (Mollusca: Gastropoda: Opisthobranchia) |journal=Chemoecology |volume=8 |issue=2 |year=1998 |pages=51–60 |doi=10.1007/PL00001804|bibcode=1998Chmec...8...51C |s2cid=41906744 }}</ref><ref name="ZhangGavagnin2007">{{cite journal |last1=Zhang |first1=Wen |last2=Gavagnin |first2=Margherita |last3=Guo |first3=Yue-Wei |last4=Mollo |first4=Ernesto |last5=Ghiselin |first5=Michael T. |last6=Cimino |first6=Guido |title=Terpenoid metabolites of the nudibranch Hexabranchus sanguineus from the South China Sea |journal=Tetrahedron |volume=63 |issue=22 |year=2007 |pages=4725–4729 |doi=10.1016/j.tet.2007.03.082}}</ref> and had both a species (''[[Hypselodoris ghiselini]]'') and the [[anti-predator adaptation|defensive chemical]] that it contains (''ghiselinin'') named after him.<ref name="HochlowskiWalker1982">{{cite journal |last1=Hochlowski |first1=Jill E. |last2=Walker |first2=Roger P. |last3=Ireland |first3=Chris |last4=Faulkner |first4=D. John |title=Metabolites of four nudibranchs of the genus Hypselodoris |journal=The Journal of Organic Chemistry |volume=47 |issue=1 |year=1982 |pages=88–91 |doi=10.1021/jo00340a018}}</ref> In 2009 he co-authored a major study on chemical defense with Guido Cimino: ''Chemical Defense and the Evolution of Opisthobranch Gastropods''.<ref>{{cite book |last1= Cimino  |first1=Guido  |first2=Michael T.  |last2=Ghiselin  |title=Chemical Defense and the Evolution of Opisthobranch Gastropods |journal=Proceedings of the California Academy of Sciences  |date=2009  |volume= 60  |issue= 10 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=r9OOQwAACAAJ|isbn=9780940228795  }}</ref>

[[File:Anemone purple anemonefish.jpg|thumb|upright|Clownfish is male when small, female when larger, an adaptation explained by Ghiselin's [[size-advantage model]].]]

In 1969 he proposed three models including the size-advantage model to explain [[sequential hermaphroditism]]. In some fish species, he reasoned, males can maximize their reproductive success by breeding with a harem of females rather than breeding only once as a female.  In other species, where the fish live in pairs, it is to an individual's advantage to be male when small and to turn into a female when it is larger.<ref name='Ghiselin'>{{cite journal | title=The evolution of hermaphroditism among animals | journal=The Quarterly Review of Biology | year=1969 | first=Michael T. | last=Ghiselin | volume=44 | pages=189–208 | pmid=4901396 | issue=2 | doi=10.1086/406066| s2cid=38139187 }}</ref>

Ghiselin worked on the history and philosophy of [[evolutionary biology]]. His historical publications dealt mainly with [[Charles Darwin|Darwin]] and the history of [[comparative anatomy|comparative zoology]]. They include such topics as the influence of alchemy on nineteenth century zoology and the history of the Zoological Station at Naples, Italy. His thought on Darwin's view of selection, whether to the individual or to the group, and sometimes apparently [[kin selection]]ist, has been criticised as inconsistent by the Darwinian philosopher [[Helena Cronin]].<ref>{{cite book |last=Cronin |first=Helena |authorlink=Helena Cronin |title=The Ant and the Peacock: Altruism and Sexual Selection from Darwin to Today |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=y0wTY3z3nggC&pg=PA305 |year=1993 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |isbn=978-0-521-45765-1 |page=305}}</ref>

His main contribution to the philosophy of biology concerns the principles of biological classification. Ghiselin is widely credited with providing the first explicit philosophical formulation of the species-as-individuals (SAI) thesis, initially proposed in 1966 and further elaborated in later works. According to this view, biological species are not merely logical classes or natural kinds, but concrete historical entities with spatiotemporal continuity.<ref>{{cite journal
 |last=Ghiselin
 |first=Michael T.
 |year=1966
 |title=On Psychologism in the Logic of Taxonomic Controversies
 |journal=Systematic Zoology
 |volume=15
 |issue=3
 |pages=207–215
 |doi=10.2307/1216613
}}</ref><ref name="Ghiselin 1974 pp. 536–544" />


Although related ideas can be traced back to earlier evolutionary thinkers, such as Haeckel’s historical conception of species and Hennig’s phylogenetic approach, Ghiselin’s contribution was to articulate these insights within a systematic philosophical framework and to establish the species-as-individuals view as a central position in debates on biological classification and philosophy of science.

He criticised the falsification of the history of [[Lamarckism|Lamarck's theory of evolution]], where in his view schoolbooks and "textbook-writers have imbued the fictitious Lamarck with an importance that the real Lamarck never had, and they have credited him with ideas that the real Lamarck did not hold. They have invented a myth in which those ideas are compared falsely with Darwin's ideas, to produce a bogus dichotomy."<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Ghiselin |first1=Michael T. |title=The Imaginary Lamarck: A Look at Bogus "History" in Schoolbooks |url=http://www.textbookleague.org/54marck.htm |journal=The Textbook Letter |issue=September–October 1994 |date=1994 |access-date=2017-05-28 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080212174536/http://www.textbookleague.org/54marck.htm |archive-date=2008-02-12 |url-status=usurped }}</ref> He has also criticized the views of [[Creationism|creationist]]s as non-scientific.<ref>[http://www.skepticfiles.org/evolut/illogicc.htm "The Illogic of Creationism An Essay Review by Michael T. Ghiselin"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170524025410/http://www.skepticfiles.org/evolut/illogicc.htm |date=2017-05-24 }}. Retrieved 1 July 2018.</ref>

His main contribution to philosophy concerns the principles of classification (systematics or taxonomy). He is given much of the credit for first theorizing that biological species are not ''kinds'' of organisms, but are rather ''individuals'' in a philosophical sense (in the manner that an individual population is an individual entity, rather than an abstract type).<ref name="Ghiselin 1974 pp. 536–544">{{cite journal |last=Ghiselin |first=M. T. |title=A Radical Solution to the Species Problem | journal=Systematic Biology |volume=23 |issue=4 |date=1 December 1974 |doi=10.1093/sysbio/23.4.536 |pages=536–544 |jstor=2412471 |url=https://philpapers.org/rec/GHIARS }}</ref> A human being is not a ''Homo sapiens'' for the same reason that [[Ontario]] is not a Canada.<ref name="Ghiselin2006">{{cite journal |last1=Ghiselin |first1=Michael T. |title=Is the Pope a Catholic? |journal=Biology & Philosophy |volume=22 |issue=2 |year=2006 |pages=283–291 |doi=10.1007/s10539-006-9045-7|s2cid=170319919 }}</ref> Ghiselin was the originator of the term "chunks of the genealogical nexus" to describe species.<ref>{{cite book |author=Ghiselin, M. T. |year=1969 |title=The triumph of the Darwinian method |url=https://archive.org/details/triumphofdarwini0000ghis |url-access=registration |publisher=University of California Press |page=[https://archive.org/details/triumphofdarwini0000ghis/page/82 82] |isbn=978-0226290249}}</ref>

Ghiselin had many interdisciplinary interests, among which was forging links between biology and [[economics]]. He was Vice President of the International Society for Bioeconomics, and served as the Co-Editor of the ''Journal of Bioeconomics'' since it was established in 1998. The first academic chair of [[Biological economics|bioeconomics]] was established at the [[University of Siena]]; as a visiting professor he was its first occupant.<ref>{{cite web |title=Invited Speakers |url=http://www3.unisi.it/eventi/darwin/speakers.htm |publisher=University of Siena |accessdate=4 February 2018 |date=10 December 2009}}</ref> As Chair of the Center for the History and Philosophy of Science his main responsibility was to organize scholarly meetings and to serve as Editor of the volumes based on them.
 
He was made a Guggenheim fellow in 1978.<ref>{{cite web |title=Michael T. Ghiselin |url=https://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/michael-t-ghiselin/ |publisher=Guggenheim Foundation |accessdate=4 February 2018}}</ref>
